The session column treated every timestamp under 24 hours old as "today", so a Session used yesterday at 22:00 and one used at 22:00 today both read `22:00`. Two identical clock-time branches also contradicted the function's comment.

## What changed
`stamp()` now compares local calendar dates, not elapsed hours. Same date keeps `HH:MM`; one day back reads `TEXT.workspace.yesterday`; 2–6 days use `daysAgo(n)`; 7+ use `weeksAgo(floor(n/7))`. Day indexes use local date components normalized to UTC, so DST cannot shift the count. The duplicated `days < 1` branch is gone.

The Issue assumed `昨天` existed, but it did not; because `Text = typeof ZH` requires parity, `workspace.yesterday` was added to both `zh.ts` and `en.ts`. The existing sidebar-extra date test was rewritten with deterministic calendar-day fixtures, with new cases for today, yesterday, day/week boundaries, invalid input, and the yesterday-22:00 render.

`SessionBar` is deliberately unchanged: it is outside this Issue's Sidebar scope, and its header describes the Session just opened, where the day is implicit. Its unconditional `HH:MM` is the same family of misreading, left as a possible follow-up.

## Validation
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck` — exit 0.

- Rendered the real Sidebar/styles in Chromium (1000×700, DPR 2).

## What changed

`clampPanelWidth` reserved 360px for a sidebar before subtracting the transcript's 512px minimum, but the sidebar is not in the row while the panel is open (`App` renders it only when the panel is closed): the panel was capped at 528px instead of 812px at 1400, 480 instead of 692 at 1280.

`panel-width.ts` now states the row's cost as `PANEL_RAIL_WIDTH` (64, `--d-rail`), `PANEL_SHELL_GUTTER` (the 6px `.main-area`/`.workspace-panel` margins) and `PANEL_SHELL_RESERVE` (76). The other constants, the nudge steps and the drag/stored-width paths are unchanged.

Stale comments now describe the live `design.css` flex shell, and both hide rules: `shell.css` at 1100px and below (`display: none !important`, still live) and `design.css` at 820px.

The issue's 320 (rail 64 + sidebar 256) is not the shell either: `.sidebar` is 296px, 256px only at 1080px and below where the panel is already hidden, and absent while the panel is open. A 320 reserve would cap the panel at 568 at 1400.

## Ownership of #1296

This PR fixes only #1395's ceiling: the width arithmetic and the comments. #1296's keyboard half stays with PR #1298 (`bot/issue-1296`): on this base `use-panel-width.ts` still clamps `nudge` against the window and writes the ceiling into the stored width, which #1298 pins. #1298 rewrites these same two files, so it has to be rebased onto this branch after this lands, and #1298 keeps #1296 as its closing issue; this PR does not claim it.

One correction for that rebase: #1298's `viewportWidth - PANEL_RAIL_WIDTH - 512` is 12px too generous because it drops the two 6px margins, leaving the transcript 500px at the ceiling. It should use `PANEL_SHELL_RESERVE` (76).

## Screenshots

Panel open at its ceiling, transcript at its floor. "Before" is the pre-fix clamp pinned as `--panel-width`: 628px at 1500, and 480px at 1280 because the old 408px ceiling is below the panel's 480px minimum.

![Before, 1500px window: rail 64, transcript 796, panel 628](https://agent-ci-infra-bot.llmbots.co/pr-media/565c9f539a618799ebc4d27b94b6eb1ac44284750e33de46c8fc8fd46eb3f62e)

Measured from the frames: at 1500 the panel goes 628 → 912 and the transcript 796 → 512; at 1280, 480 → 692 and 724 → 512. The rail and the two 6px gutters are 76px in every frame.

- Headless Chromium over the repository's `index.css`, panel at its ceiling: 1400 → rail 64, main 512, panel 812; 1280 → 692; 1688 → 1100; 1101 → 513; row sums to the viewport, no overflow; `display: none` at 1100 and below.

1424.author: agent-ci-infra-bot[bot]
1424.body:
Archiving, deleting or switching a Session's approval mode used a fresh runner `/health` probe as the guard for `teardownKernels`, and swallowed probe failures with `.catch(() => undefined)`. ## Changes
- `services/api/src/http/index.ts`: added `teardownSessionKernels`, which always calls the idempotent `runnerClient.teardownKernels` and, on failure, logs `session_kernel_teardown_failed` with `sessionId` and `errorMessage` (same shape as `sandbox_network_teardown_failed`).
- Archive, delete and approval-mode now use it unconditionally. Delete attempts teardown before the Session record disappears; approval-mode still records the teardown reason in its audit entry only when the count is known.
- New `services/api/src/session-kernel-teardown.test.ts` drives the public routes against a Runner stub.

## Validation
- Regression test on the candidate: 2 of 2 passed. On baseline `645dc7ba3`: 0 of 2 passed (health 503 skipped all three teardowns; a failed teardown answered 500 instead of 200 + warn).
- Related existing API tests (Session/Project lifecycle, delete mirror, archived-session integration): 4 of 4 passed.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api typecheck` and `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json`: clean.
- UT (sandbox-free subset): 8074 planned / 8074 executed / 8068 passed / 6 failed, all host-attributed outside this change (no bubblewrap/userns, no NPU, runner gates; one timing test passes in isolation).
- ST model:mock subset: 32/32 executed, 31 passed, 1 failed with `ENOENT: realpath 'bwrap'`.
- Full `pnpm ci:ut` / `ci:st` / `ci:e2e` cannot start on this host: preflight reports `BUBBLEWRAP_UNAVAILABLE` (user namespaces denied, no root to install setuid bwrap); `ci:e2e` also lacks the `.e2e` Playwright install. CI runs all layers.

## Release
Release category: release:fix
User impact: kernel teardown is no longer skipped when the Runner probe is failing, and teardown failures are logged instead of hidden.
Compatibility and migration: none.

The Evolve create dialog trusted a runtime status read once. `use-evolve.ts` stopped polling at `ready` and `refreshStatus()` had no caller, so a dead sidecar still showed 就绪, hid the "runtime cannot run the search" banner and left 开始设计 enabled — a design turn paid for a runtime that could not run it.

## What changed
- A ready runtime is re-read every 45 s (unready keeps the 4 s cadence), and at most one status read is in flight, so an older `ready` cannot land after a newer `error`. Timers and the listener are cleared on unmount, and hidden windows stop polling.
- Failures are no longer sticky: one failed read is tolerated, two consecutive ones stop showing the runtime as ready, and any success restores it.
- The dialog re-reads on open (`onRefreshStatus` from `App`), so a dead sidecar yields the banner and a disabled 开始设计.

1426.author: moShangLouTou
1426.body:
Idea Tree ideation receives `maxDepth` and node depths but has to infer how many direction and refinement levels fit beneath each selected parent. Over-deep proposals are safely trimmed, but their intermediate research structure can be lost.

This change sends `selectedParentConstraints` with each selected parent’s remaining depth, intermediate-path allowance, direction requirements, and maximum refinement count. The ideation prompt explains reserving one level for the candidate and compressing the hierarchy while retaining scientific constraints in the hypothesis. Budgets reuse the insertion path helpers, including ROOT and last-level candidate behavior, and remain present during correction requests. Existing backend trimming and validation remain in place.

Related to #1327; complements #1297 and #1392 by guiding generation before the safety trim.

Validation:
- `PYTHONPATH=services/evolve/src services/evolve/.venv/bin/python -m pytest services/evolve/tests/test_idea_research.py -q`: 46 passed, 6 subtests passed. Covers ROOT, direction and completed-candidate parents, depth-3 and last-level budgets, and delivery across initial/corrected ideation requests. Direct invocation emits the existing unregistered `science_tags` marker warning.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Real-model adherence to the new guidance has not been evaluated.
